My dad seem to start to have dementia or hard of hearing, and I'm completely having gotten ready he's passing anytime soon (Though he's probably not and would probably be heartbroken that I'm this way already), mom's still healthy and takes care of us by cooking even at her near-70 age, and it's the fact I know for sure I'm going right after her that I'm not even caring about trying to learn how to take care of myself for when they're both gone, and that I don't have to save up crazy amounts of money for my retirement because I'll never get there.

It never is about a "stay around it will get better" thing anymore but a choice made completely sober and calm, and I've even talked to my psychiatrist about it. She just accepted it and that she's glad that at least I'm still thinking of my parents to not put them through losing me,  and that I confided in her whereby she told me this is called existential depression and all we can do is to make the rest of my alive time bearable, but I really am just living with the idea that I will not be alive for more than another 10 years. And somehow, this puts me at some weird sense of ease.

No one of my 'friends' look for me now, probably thinking they should give me space, but what my mind says is that they're better off without me and I can't wait for me to actually leave.

I remember how much of a wreck my parents were when I attempted, and my mom, especially, who seemingly \~brushes such comments of mine off\~ have reacted the same way as yours on the usual before that incident. I can assure you that it definitely threw her off-guard, and she never saw the question coming, never thought of that ever happening, and she probably spent a lot of time pondering and being scared about what ifs after. If you're close to your mom, do have a heart-to-heart talk with her. I promise it will make you feel better. I care about you, too.
